newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The major banks have appealed to the Reserve Bank to help avert another increase in prime overdraft rates by easing pressure in the money market.
- Negotiations with three potential black empowerment bidders for the sale of Anglo American's 47 percent stake in mining house JCI Ltd might be concluded this week, sources said at the week-end.
- State-owned resort company Aventura is mired in a cash flow crisis and has appealed to government to guarantee a six million rand bridging finance loan to cover capital and operating costs.

- The SA Police Service is planning a major restructuring programme which could see many logistics and administrative functions outsourced and up to 35,000 uniformed personnel transferred to core policing duties.

- The Gabonese doctor who brought the dreaded Ebola virus into Gauteng has recovered and been discharged from hospital, while the Sandton nurse who contracted the disease while treating him remains in a critical condition in the Johannesburg Hospital.
- A 350 million rand golf estate and hotel development will be built in Knysna by Thailand-based PK Developments.

- Capital Alliance Holdings (formerly AGA Holdings), which reported attributable income of 25 million rand for the six months to September 30, is set to establish a new fund dedicated to mining investments, Mzi Khumalo, the Capital Alliance executive chairman, said on Friday.

- JCI Ltd is considering restructuring its minerals assets along te same lines as rival mining house Anglovaal Minerals, but only after Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's stake in JCI has been sold to black investors.
- The Transport and General Workers' Union rejected a revised offer from the Road Freight Association on Friday and served notice on Monday that a strike would start on Wednesday.
- A black consortium has acquired a 51 percent stake in Tolcon, the toll road operation and maintenance company owned by M&R Contractors, for an undisclosed amount.
- Johannesburg doctors worked around the clock to identify a Gabon doctor as the person who infected 46-year old theatre nurse Marilyn Lahana with the deadly Ebola virus.
